messages:
Maria (CS): AcmeCorp reported ~20 users (mostly service accounts) suddenly lost the 'analytics' role after their IdP domain merge. They can still auth but missing role permissions. Anyone seen this pattern?
Ethan (Support): Upload of their SCIM logs shows successful user updates but group->role mapping empty for the affected accounts. Can you share an example user and timestamps?
AcmeCorp Admin: example svc: svc-reports@acme.com. We see SCIM PATCHs around 2026-02-14T08:12Z that look fine. Post-merge their user entries now have externalId set to `saml:acme:12345` instead of original `acme-12345`. Roles in console are gone.
Ethan (Support): Hmm — could be externalId namespace normalization after SSO org merge. Our mapping rules use raw externalId equality to attach groups -> roles. If externalId prefixes changed, mapping can break.
AcmeCorp Admin: We did a domain consolidation and IdP team prefixed some externalIds. We didn't expect that to change our SCIM payloads.
scim-bot: Received webhook: PATCH /Users/abc123; status=200; body: { "id": "abc123", "externalId": "saml:acme:12345", "groups": [] }
Ivan (Identity): Quick check — are these service accounts being created by SSO-linked provisioning or by a separate service account flow? If they're SSO-linked, the connector token needs both `scim:write:users` and `scim:write:groups` scopes to maintain group assignments. If token only has `scim:write:users` we accept user updates but drop group assignment changes.
Maria (CS): Acme supplied the connector token. They said it was the same token used before merge. Could the IdP change cause token scope changes?
Ethan (Support): Token scopes wouldn't change spontaneously. But our logs show an intermittent 403 when applying group patches for these accounts right after merge window. Excerpt from infra logs:
```
[2026-02-14T08:12:05Z] scim-connector[worker-7] PATCH /Groups/analytics/members -> 403 Forbidden (missing scope: scim:write:groups)
[2026-02-14T08:12:06Z] scim-connector[worker-7] PATCH /Users/abc123 -> 200 OK
```
Ivan (Identity): That matches scenario where user update succeeds but group patch fails, leaving user with no groups. Could be the connector re-provisioned with a different token at merge time. Ask Acme: did you re-run the connector or rotate tokens around the merge?
AcmeCorp Admin: We rotated the connector token as part of the migration (we thought it was required). We didn't realize groups scope was separate.
Jamie (SRE): For remediation we should: 1) confirm current connector token scopes, 2) reapply missing group mappings for affected users, 3) backfill for any accounts where externalId changed.
Ethan (Support): Repro steps I ran:
1) GET /v1/scim/Users?filter=externalId eq "saml:acme:12345" -> returns user id abc123
2) GET /v1/scim/Users/abc123 -> shows `groups: []`
3) Attempted PATCH /v1/scim/Groups/analytics with members add -> 403 when token lacks `scim:write:groups`.
Command used:
```
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer <connector-token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/scim/Groups/analytics \
  -d '{ "Operations": [{"op":"add","path":"members","value":[{"value":"abc123"}]}] }'
```
AcmeCorp Admin: Confirmed the rotated token was created by our IdP automation and only granted user write perms. Oops.
Maria (CS): For immediate fix can we re-run a backfill to reattach roles for users whose externalId changed? We'll need to normalize externalId mapping.
Jamie (SRE): Proposed immediate steps (short term):
- Ivan: verify connector token scopes and request a new token with `scim:write:groups` if missing.
- Ethan: run a one-off backfill: iterate affected externalId prefixes and re-run group membership patches. Script outline: POST /internal/scim/backfill with body `{"externalId_prefix": "saml:acme:"}` (internal endpoint requires eng approval).
- Maria: ask Acme if they can temporarily re-run connector with old token (if safe) while we backfill.
Ivan (Identity): Longer term: update our SCIM onboarding docs to warn about externalId namespace changes and enforce connector scope validation at registration time. Also track when tokens are rotated in connector audit logs.
Ethan (Support): I ran a minimal backfill for Acme (dev environment) and it worked: members reattached when using token with `scim:write:groups`. Example success log:
```
[2026-02-14T10:03:12Z] backfill-job[acme] reattach user abc123 -> 204 No Content
[2026-02-14T10:03:12Z] scim-connector[worker-2] PATCH /Groups/analytics -> 204 No Content
```
AcmeCorp Admin: We can request a new token with the proper scopes and authorize a backfill. Please proceed, this affects scheduled reports.
Maria (CS): I'll coordinate and get written consent for backfill. Can we get eng support to review the backfill endpoint (internal) and run it?
Jamie (SRE): Looping eng oncall: @Jamie (SRE) assigned to run and monitor backfill during low traffic. I'll also add a small migration tool to normalize externalId prefixes for the tenant namespace (safe id mapping + audit).
Ivan (Identity): I'll add a pre-check to connector registration to validate `scim:write:groups` is present for orgs that have group->role mappings.
Ethan (Support): Marking this P1 for Acme (enterprise SLA). Next steps: Maria to collect consent + confirm token OR provide new token; Ivan to validate scopes; Jamie to run backfill; Ethan to monitor and confirm roles restored.
Maria (CS): Consent received from Acme. They provided a new token with full scim scopes. Please proceed. :thumbsup:
Jamie (SRE): Running backfill now, will post progress. :eyes:
scim-bot: backfill job started for tenant acme at 2026-02-14T22:05Z (job id bf-20260214-01)
Jamie (SRE): Backfill completed. I spot-checked 10 users, roles restored and scheduled reports resumed. Closing loop with Acme.
AcmeCorp Admin: Thanks team! Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Maria (CS): I'll update the customer notes and add a KB: "SCIM connectors + IdP merges: token scopes & externalId normalization".
